chunks: With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Faddal, from a man, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family) said: Openhandedness is a tree whose root is in Paradise and which shades upon this world. The one who adheres to a branch of it will be drawn to Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of openhandedness in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Maani al-Akhbar, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to illustrate the metaphysical reality of generosity, portraying it not merely as a social virtue but as a tangible spiritual entity rooted in Jannah. This imagery emphasizes that the act of giving creates a direct ontological link between the donor's conduct in the temporal world and their ultimate abode, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on character (akhlaq) as a means of salvation.
